details.description: DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat is the supervised-fine-tuned chat version of DeepSeek-V2-Lite, a 16-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 2.4 billion parameters activated per token, which DeepSeek released in May 2024. It uses DeepSeek's Multi-head Latent Attention to compress its key-value cache and DeepSeekMoE for sparse, economical computation; DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card says these let it run BF16 inference on a single 40GB GPU. It is the smaller sibling of the 236-billion-parameter DeepSeek-V2-Chat in the same model family. Model use is governed by DeepSeek's Model License, while the DeepSeek-V2 code is released under the MIT License.
advantages: Supports a 163,840-token context window via YaRN RoPE scaling, per its Hugging Face configuration file.
Scores 57.3 on HumanEval, per DeepSeek's official DeepSeek-V2 GitHub repository.
Scores 72.0 on GSM8K, per DeepSeek's DeepSeek-V2 GitHub repository.
Scores 55.7 on MMLU, per DeepSeek's DeepSeek-V2 GitHub repository.
Uses Multi-head Latent Attention and DeepSeekMoE so it can run BF16 inference on a single 40GB GPU, per its Hugging Face model card.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's GitHub repository says the open-source Hugging Face Transformers implementation runs slower than DeepSeek's internal codebase, and recommends vLLM for best performance.
Text-only chat model; its model card documents no vision or tool-use support.
use_cases: Deployment in memory-constrained settings that only fit a single 40GB GPU.

notes: Catalog's max_input/output tokens (163840) match this model's max_position_embeddings in its Hugging Face config.json (reached via YaRN RoPE scaling from a 4,096-token base). However, DeepSeek's own model table on that same Hugging Face page, and its GitHub README's model table, both list this model's documented context length as 32K, not 163840 -- kept the catalog's figure per instructions and flagging this disagreement here. No maker source marks this model deprecated; it remains part of DeepSeek's May 2024 V2 release, since followed by larger DeepSeek model generations.
